Mac OS X Aqua interface

Apple’s water-themed interface: gel buttons, droplet controls, and reflective surfaces that set up the gloss of the later style.

Source
Wikipedia: Aqua (user interface)
Creator
Apple
Made
Introduced January 2000; first released July 2000 with iMovie 2 and in Mac OS X 10.0 in 2001
Style
Frutiger Aero (precursor; agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Glossy, liquid, playful
Evidence
Inspected two non-free screenshots in scratchpad copies: File:Macosxpb.png (Mac OS X Public Beta, 365 × 273) and File:Leopard Desktop.png (Mac OS X Leopard, 800 × 500). Not stored.

Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Aqua “was themed to replicate water, with ‘droplet-like’ components and a heavy use of reflective effects and translucency.” It was introduced at Macworld in January 2000, first shipped with iMovie 2 in July 2000, and with Mac OS X 10.0 the following year. Wikipedia: Aqua).

Before OS X Yosemite (2014), most Aqua controls had a “glass” or “gel” effect. Apple moved to flat design in 2013. Wikipedia: Aqua).

CARI lists “Aqua” as an alternate name for Frutiger Aero. CARI: Frutiger Aero.

Observed

  • Public Beta (2000): windows have pinstriped gray bars, red, yellow, and green gel buttons, and translucent blue highlighted menu items.
  • Public Beta: the Dock at the bottom holds glossy, shaded icons on a translucent strip.
  • Leopard (2007): the desktop picture is a magenta and violet aurora with stars; the Dock is a reflective glass shelf with icons mirrored below.
  • Leopard: window chrome is gray and brushed rather than pinstriped; blue folder icons are soft and rounded.

Why it belongs

Aqua supplies the gloss, gel, and reflection. Frutiger Aero adds bright daylight nature imagery and humanist type to that surface. Leopard’s aurora picture shows the two converging by 2007.

Borrow

Use a floor reflection under a row of icons to suggest a glass shelf.

Give small status buttons a gel look: saturated color, a white highlight, and a dark rim.
